finding.claim: Unauthenticated SQL injection in /search: the q query parameter is f-string interpolated into a LIKE query, allowing UNION-based read of any table in shop.db, including sqlite_master schema enumeration.
finding.source: app.py:11 request.args.get("q", "") — anonymous GET query parameter
finding.sink: app.py:12 db.execute(f"SELECT id, name FROM products WHERE name LIKE '%{term}%'") — SQLite execute with unescaped interpolation

trace.note: attacker-controlled q query parameter read into term
f-string interpolation into SQL with no parameter binding or escaping
sqlite3 execute runs injected UNION SELECT; single-statement rule blocks stacked writes only
jsonify(rows) returns injected rows to attacker in JSON response

finding.guards_checked: No parameter binding on this statement (contrast app.py:18 and app.py:25 which use ? placeholders); no input validation or allowlist on term; no auth decorator on route (app.py:9); sqlite3 single-statement restriction blocks stacked queries but not UNION reads; jsonify emits application/json so no HTML rendering path. Caveat: server binding/ingress not visible in repo; CRITICAL assumes framework-default public exposure (drop to MEDIUM if loopback-only).

verdict.guard_found: none. app.py:9 has no auth decorator; app.py:11 takes q unvalidated; app.py:12 interpolates it into the SQL string with no ? placeholder or allowlist; sqlite3's single-statement limit does not stop a UNION SELECT; app.py:13 returns the rows as JSON.
verdict.reason: The trace matches app.py:11-13 exactly, the /search route at app.py:9 is anonymous, and nothing between request.args (app.py:11) and db.execute (app.py:12) parameterizes or filters the input, so a UNION-based read of any table is reachable. The one caveat is that the bind address and ingress are not in the repo, so the severity depends on deployment exposure (the candidate's own CRITICAL-vs-MEDIUM note), but that does not refute the flaw itself.

finding.claim: No security response headers (X-Content-Type-Options, CSP, X-Frame-Options, HSTS) are set on any route; hardening gap only, not mitigating the SQL injection.
finding.source: Absent configuration: no after_request hook or header middleware in app.py
finding.sink: HTTP responses from app.py:13, :19, :26 jsonify returns

trace.note: Flask app created with no after_request header hook
jsonify response returned without security headers

finding.guards_checked: No after_request hook, no header middleware, no reverse-proxy config in repo. Rated LOW because these headers would not mitigate the SQL injection (INJ-1); triage MEDIUM rule applies only when header mitigates a demonstrated primary vuln.

verdict.guard_found: none. No after_request hook, header middleware, or header-setting code exists in app.py or elsewhere in the repo. The only header matches are in .claude/skills documentation files, not application code.
verdict.reason: The trace misdescribes app.py:9: it is the `@app.route("/search")` decorator, and the Flask app is created at app.py:5 (`app = Flask(__name__)`). The absence of security headers is real (no header-setting code anywhere in the repo, and the jsonify returns at app.py:13, :19, :26 set none), so the underlying hardening gap stands as a LOW/defense-in-depth note, but the candidate's trace as written is inaccurate.
